decisions.reason: The cross-Requirement effect is already fully represented by the candidate's message-567 MODIFY, including removal of the onboard level shifter and use of a future adapter board.
The source decision concerns sensor-board interfaces and explicitly limits the conclusion to connected sensors; it does not change the separately established LED power or data-level interface.
Sensor logic-level compatibility does not change the standalone USB regulator, its source-selection behavior, or the loads powered by the 3.3V rail.
Skipping the sensor-board level-shifter footprint does not alter the established interboard connector types, pinouts, power chain, or signal routes.
The source confirms sensor logic compatibility but does not change DCDC1 voltage regulation, current capacity, compensation, or its 3.3V-rail role.
The SPS30 and ZE08 remain 5V-powered loads despite using 3.3V-compatible logic, so the monitored rails and current-monitoring topology remain unchanged.
The sensor level-shifter decision has no semantic effect on the passive buzzer type, voltage compatibility, sourcing, or selected part.
The source addresses level shifting for sensor connectors, not the LED daughterboard's supply, part selection, or physical configuration.
Eliminating an optional logic-level shifter does not change the I2C pull-ups, series resistors, bus speed, cable assumptions, or signal-conditioning topology.
The source retains the existing sensor and spare connectors and changes only the level-shifting strategy, so the connector fanout remains valid unchanged.
The source explicitly confirms that SPS30 and ZE08 remain 5V-powered; only their logic compatibility is discussed, leaving the switchable 5V rail unchanged.
This candidate concerns power-board BOM readiness, while the removed level-shifter footprint belongs to the sensor-board interface and does not alter the candidate's current BOM attributes.
